author: bronek_90134
content: the problem with 4 is that there is no space left in cache at the time when a bottom tree is about to change - a client would build a new bottom keytree in advance (it's an expensive operation, especially for a VC holding large number of keys) and there would be, every 8192 slots, more than 4 key trees that need to be readily available (current and new). Grandine has a workaround for this by carefully ordering key tree accesses, go-leanxmss dafaults to 8.

author: bronek_90134
content: I am being corrected that at the time of change there would be no **slack** - all 4 slots would be used.  The cache evicts the least recently used tree, and that means 3 are kept in memory and one can be lost and will need to be rebuilt - unless a client took care to copy it aside. Meaning even 5 or  6 would do.

author: t.wambsgans

author: bronek_90134
content:
Cache is per key; number of keys doesn't change the cache size needed, only the total memory used. I am calculating that generation of 500 keytrees on 0.19.0 would need ~ 2.5 to 3 minutes of single core work with AVX512 ; estimated 2x - 3x higher on AVX2 only. Assuming 8x parallelism it's less but still a significant amount of work, so any VC would likely spread that over time, meaning it would have to keep keytrees in cache. For 500 keys, cache sized to 4 is 10.5MB, I hope an extra 10.5MB for 4 more keytrees is not unreasonable burden (a bottom keytree needs 5300 bytes).

Also leanVM 0.19.0 has a `LeanXmssExpandedSecretKey::set_bottom_tree_cache_size` to set it at runtime, I think 6 would be a reasonable number - it does not need to be a power of 2.

author: bronek_90134
content: FWIW keytree generation is trivially parallelizable across keys; even within a single key the serial part is tiny
